analysis.summary: ESLint 8.55.0 uses the legacy .eslintrc.cjs file format; ESLint 9 drops legacy config in favor of flat config (eslint.config.js or .mjs). The current config is small (no overrides, no per-file rules, no custom parsers), so the migration is mostly mechanical with `@eslint/migrate-config` or a hand-written flat config that uses FlatCompat for the prettier/react presets. Closes F-DEP-008.
analysis.details: Current implementation: .eslintrc.cjs is module.exports with four extends, parserOptions.ecmaVersion 'latest' + sourceType 'module' + jsx, plugins [react, react-hooks], settings.react.version 'detect', four rules, and ignorePatterns [dist, node_modules, *.config.js]. The 'lint' npm script is `eslint src/` which is already a directory glob, so no script change is needed. The migration path: replace .eslintrc.cjs with eslint.config.js (or .mjs) that uses FlatCompat to import the four extends and applies the same four rules. eslint-plugin-react v7.33.2 predates flat config support; v8 is the first flat-config-compatible release. eslint-plugin-react-hooks v4.6.0 also predates flat config; v5 is the matching release. The Plan task name 'npx @eslint/migrate-config .eslintrc.cjs' is the official helper; output is a starting eslint.config.js that still needs manual review for the FlatCompat wrapper. Verification per the issue body: `npm run lint` exits 0 and the tests still pass. Risk: dropping legacy config breaks the lint step before the flat config is added, so the PR must land both files in a single commit (or stage the new file before deleting the old one). The .eslintrc.cjs ignore pattern `*.config.js` is interesting — it means Vite's vite.config.js is currently excluded, and that must be preserved in flat config via `ignores`.

options.name: Flat config via FlatCompat (recommended for minimal churn)
options.summary: Generate eslint.config.mjs (or .js) that imports FlatCompat and re-emits the same four extends, plugins, rules, and ignores. Bump eslint ^9, eslint-plugin-react ^8, eslint-plugin-react-hooks ^5, eslint-config-prettier ^10. Delete .eslintrc.cjs in the same commit.
pros: Closest 1:1 translation of the current config
cons: FlatCompat is a transitional helper; future ESLint majors may deprecate it
Plugin v8/v5 have minor breaking changes worth checking
options.risk_details: Plugins and presets all have flat-config-aware releases; risk is mostly rule-shape churn (e.g. react-hooks v5 renamed a rule) and the FlatCompat version pin.

options.name: Hand-written flat config (no FlatCompat)
options.summary: Write eslint.config.js from scratch with native flat-config entries (no FlatCompat). More native but requires re-emitting each rule/preset by hand.
cons: More manual translation, more places to make mistakes
options.risk_details: Same as Option 1, plus higher chance of mis-mapping a preset.

decision_record.root_cause: ESLint 8 uses legacy .eslintrc.* config; ESLint 9 mandates flat config, and the project still on 8 is a DEP finding.
options_considered: Flat config via FlatCompat (recommended for minimal churn)
decision_record.selected_option: Flat config via FlatCompat (recommended for minimal churn)
decision_record.residual_risk: FlatCompat is transitional; if a future ESLint major drops it, a second migration is required.
